title: 12. Reverse Linked List (In-Place Pointers)
description:
Given the head of a singly linked list represented as a standard list of integer values `values` (e.g. `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`), reverse the list and return the reversed list of values (`[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]`).

Your solution should simulate the in-place pointer redirect `curr.next = prev` rather than simply calling Python's built-in `values[::-1]`.
constraints:
• 0 <= len(values) <= 5000
• -5000 <= values[i] <= 5000
• Optimal Time: O(N) | Optimal Space: O(1) auxiliary
solution:
def reverse_list(values: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    if not values:
        return []
    # Simulation of linked list node pointer redirect
    class Node:
        def __init__(self, v):
            self.val = v
            self.next = None
    head = Node(values[0])
    curr = head
    for v in values[1:]:
        curr.next = Node(v)
        curr = curr.next
    # In-place reversal
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    # Collect reversed
    res = []
    curr = prev
    while curr:
        res.append(curr.val)
        curr = curr.next
    return res
explanation: Iterative reversal maintains three pointers (`prev`, `curr`, `nxt`). At each step, `curr.next` is redirected to `prev`. Advancing `prev = curr` and `curr = nxt` reverses all pointers in a single pass O(N) with O(1) auxiliary space.
